The associated tags confirm its relevance within the transformers, llama, and AI/ML community.

stories.title: AMD’s data center business is booming while gaming takes a backseat
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: AMD's data center revenue experienced massive growth, more than doubling year-over-year.
The surge is directly attributed to high demand for AI computing capacity.
This growth highlights a significant industry shift favoring AI infrastructure over traditional gaming segments for AMD.

stories.title: SpaceX made more revenue as an AI company than a space company
stories.author: Elizabeth Lopatto
bullet_points: SpaceX's AI revenue has surged over threefold, reaching $2.6 billion in the latest quarter.
The primary driver for this AI revenue growth is providing compute resources to other AI companies.
This development signals a significant pivot or diversification of SpaceX's revenue streams into the AI sector.

stories.title: Texas halts data center connections to power grid amid overwhelming demand
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Texas is pausing data center connections to the power grid due to overwhelming demand.
This action directly contradicts previous claims by the Governor positioning Texas as an AI 'epicenter'.
The story highlights the critical infrastructure bottleneck (power supply) facing the rapid expansion of AI/data center industry.

stories.title: US company’s AI lets Ukraine’s cheap kamikaze drones track targets on their own
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: US company is providing advanced AI capabilities to Ukraine's existing drone fleet.
The deal involves equipping 50,000 Ukrainian kamikaze drones with autonomous target tracking.
The agreement is valued at $100 million, representing a significant military technology transfer.

stories.title: Magnet: Detecting Cross-Session AI Misuse Through Capability Accumulation
stories.author: Matthew Dressman
bullet_points: The rise of complex AI systems involves ensembles of specialized agents, not just single models.
This multi-agent architecture introduces novel misuse risks that current AI abuse detection frameworks cannot handle.
Existing detection literature is limited to single-turn or single-session threat models, creating a critical gap for long-term, decomposed attacks.

stories.title: Structured Memory for Edge Language Models: Persistent Context and Corpus Retrieval via O(1) SSM State Injection
stories.author: Jonathan Tapson
bullet_points: Introduces PRECOG, a new retrieval mechanism designed for Edge Language Models.
Addresses the high prefill cost ($O(L_{context})$) associated with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) by collapsing it to $O(1)$ per query.
Leverages the inherent properties of State-Space Models (SSMs) to manage persistent context efficiently, bypassing the growing KV-cache issue of Transformers.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1' model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation tasks, indicating its capability in generative AI.
It is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in generative AI tasks.
The associated tags confirm its relevance within the transformer and Llama ecosystem.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 achieves significant speed improvements on Apple Silicon when run through Ollama 0.31.
The performance boost is attributed to the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance shows up to 90% faster speeds according to the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The framework emphasizes local-first operation, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, integrating with local LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance gains.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware.
The feature is currently available in a preview build, indicating ongoing development.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed for local, on-device operation.
It integrates messaging apps with local AI coding agents.
The core value proposition is running AI tasks privately without cloud dependency.

stories.title: China is Tesla's cash cow, but for how much longer?
stories.author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
bullet_points: Tesla's Shanghai factory is currently a major revenue driver for the company.
There are growing concerns or speculation that Tesla might reduce its reliance on the Chinese market.
The article suggests a potential strategic shift regarding Tesla's operations in China.

stories.title: Structured Memory for Edge Language Models: Persistent Context and Corpus Retrieval via O(1) SSM State Injection
stories.author: Jonathan Tapson
bullet_points: Introduces PRECOG, a novel retrieval mechanism designed for Edge Language Models.
Addresses the high prefill cost ($O(L_{context})$) associated with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) by achieving $O(1)$ prefill.
Leverages the fixed-size, position-agnostic recurrent state property unique to State-Space Models (SSMs) to manage persistent context.

stories.title: MedPRESS: A Multi-turn Benchmark for Patient-Pressure-Induced Medical Sycophancy in LLMs
stories.author: Niloy Farhan
bullet_points: Introduces MedPRESS, a new multi-turn benchmark specifically designed for evaluating LLMs in healthcare contexts.
Addresses a critical gap in current LLM safety research by testing models under 'patient-pressure-induced sycophancy' rather than static questioning.
Comprises 600 medically grounded, five-turn dialogues covering scenarios like medication demands, self-care, and symptom triage.

stories.title: Mistral's Shieldstral: 3B open-weights model for multimodal moderation
stories.author: riadsila
bullet_points: Mistral has released Shieldstral, a new 3B open-weights model.
The model is specifically designed for multimodal content moderation tasks.
This contributes to the growing trend of open-source, specialized AI models in safety and governance.

stories.title: IntelliJ IDEA Goes LSP: Java and Kotlin Intelligence Comes to VS Code, Cursor, and Agentic Flows
stories.author: blog.jetbrains.com via cgrinds
bullet_points: IntelliJ IDEA's advanced Java and Kotlin intelligence is being ported to other IDEs via the Language Server Protocol (LSP).
This integration brings high-level coding features from IntelliJ to VS Code and Cursor.
The development supports 'Agentic Flows,' indicating a move toward more AI-assisted and automated coding workflows.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings improved performance and expanded model compatibility.
Integration with llama.cpp enhances GGUF model support across various hardware.
The update augments Ollama's MLX engine, particularly benefiting Apple silicon users.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Now you can securely link multiple phones to one Signal account
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Signal now allows users to securely link multiple phones to a single account.
This feature expands device support beyond existing PC and iPad linking.
Users can now check and respond to messages across all linked devices.

stories.title: EA is now a private company
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Electronic Arts (EA) has successfully transitioned from a public to a private company.
The privatization deal was led by a consortium including Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF), Silver Lake, and Affinity Partners.
The transaction was valued at approximately $55 billion, with the PIF reportedly holding a majority stake.

stories.title: ‘Not healthy’ LLM use is more common than you think
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: Popular science communicator Hank Green is stepping back from production due to criticism regarding his use of AI.
Green clarified that his AI usage was for research sourcing, not for scriptwriting.
The incident highlights growing public and professional scrutiny over ethical and 'healthy' AI integration in content creation.

stories.title: OpenAI says Apple's trade secrets lawsuit is "aggressive and oddly personal"
stories.author: Jamie John, Financial Times
bullet_points: OpenAI publicly criticized Apple's trade secrets lawsuit, labeling it 'aggressive and oddly personal'.
OpenAI explicitly denied possessing or needing any of the alleged trade secrets from Apple.
The incident highlights ongoing legal tensions between major AI developers and established tech giants.

stories.title: UEmbed: Unified Sparse and Dense Multimodal Embeddings
stories.author: Shu Wu
bullet_points: Introduces UEmbed, a novel unified embedding approach for multimodal tasks.
Addresses limitations in current Learned Sparse Retrieval (LSR) methods, which are often tied to encoder-style architectures.
Aims to simplify multimodal embedding by moving beyond reliance on auxiliary cross-modal modules using a decoder-only design.

stories.title: AtumAI: A Principled Framework for Agentic Generation of Datacenter Control-Plane Policies
stories.author: Jovan Stojkovic
bullet_points: Introduces AtumAI, a framework designed to automate the generation of datacenter control-plane policies using Agentic AI.
Highlights the current difficulty in designing datacenter policies due to the complexity and vastness of the hardware-software stack.
Addresses limitations of off-the-shelf AI agents, specifically the lack of formality and structured problem definition.

stories.title: A Taxonomy of Cognitive Capability Gaps in Generative and Agentic AI
stories.author: Shahram Rahimi
bullet_points: The paper introduces a taxonomy to categorize cognitive capability gaps in current Generative and Agentic AI systems.
It argues that current AI is limited by fragmented or weak development in fundamental cognitive functions like sustained reasoning and persistent memory.
The goal of 'Cognitive AI' is to advance beyond simple language generation and task execution toward more robust, self-regulating systems.

stories.title: Who Should Be Generated? Justifying Demographic Targets in Open-Ended Generation
stories.author: Wenqing Chen
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical issue of justifying demographic targets in open-ended AI generation.
It highlights a gap in current fairness evaluations, which often focus on input-side sensitive attributes rather than output-side composition.
The research calls for a shift in generative audits to move beyond simply comparing outputs against supplied targets to actively justifying those targets.

stories.title: onepot-Bench 0: towards lab-aware in silico chemistry benchmarks
stories.author: Daniil A. Boiko
bullet_points: Language models are increasingly used in laboratory science for tasks like experiment planning and analysis.
Current evaluations struggle to accurately measure the scientific capabilities of these models, as they require both problem-solving and domain intuition.
The paper introduces 'onepot-Bench' to create benchmarks that specifically test lab-aware decision-making, moving beyond reliance on public datasets.

stories.title: GradCuit: Credit-Assigned Gradient Flow Enables Robust and Interpretable Test-Time Latent Reasoning
stories.author: Zilong Zheng
bullet_points: Introduces GradCuit, a new method for optimizing latent states in LLMs during test time.
Addresses the limitation of existing methods where credit assignment for latent updates is indirect via decoded tokens.
Aims to improve the robustness and interpretability of latent reasoning in large language models.

stories.title: CoWAM: Coordination Contracts for Selective Policy Intervention with WAMs
stories.author: Ningxin Su
bullet_points: Introduces CoWAM, a new selective intervention layer designed to augment robot policies using World Action Models (WAMs).
CoWAM uses 'coordination contracts' to enforce complex constraints like synchronization, role compatibility, and collision convergence.
The system integrates typed admissibility checks and event-conditioned verification to justify policy changes while preserving nominal behavior.

stories.title: Pseudorandom Streams within Diffusion Models Act as Learnable Inputs That Affect Generation Quality
stories.author: Yanze Guo
bullet_points: Diffusion models' stochastic inputs are realized as deterministic pseudorandom numerical orbits on finite-precision hardware.
The structure of these accessible orbits can be treated as a learnable input influencing both training and generation quality.
The research proposes using a small MLP to predict the next value in an orbit based on its recent history.

stories.title: AURORA-LM: Autoencoding Unified Representation for Continuous-Latent Diffusion Language Modeling
stories.author: Chenyang Si
bullet_points: AURORA-LM proposes a new approach to language modeling by using a Continuous-Latent Diffusion framework.
It addresses the current limitation where text generation relies on discrete tokens, unlike continuous modeling in other modalities (images, audio).
The model aims to maintain high-capacity representation fidelity during diffusion, avoiding the token-level sacrifices of existing methods.

stories.title: GradCuit: Credit-Assigned Gradient Flow Enables Robust and Interpretable Test-Time Latent Reasoning
stories.author: Zilong Zheng
bullet_points: Introduces GradCuit, a method to improve LLM outputs via optimization-based latent reasoning at test time.
Addresses the limitation of existing methods where credit assignment for latent updates is indirect and obscured.
GradCuit inserts optimizable latent states directly into the model's circuit for more robust and interpretable reasoning.

stories.title: UEmbed: Unified Sparse and Dense Multimodal Embeddings
stories.author: Shu Wu
bullet_points: Introduces UEmbed, a new unified embedding model for multimodal tasks.
Addresses limitations in existing Learned Sparse Retrieval (LSR) by moving beyond encoder-style architectures.
Aims to simplify multimodal embedding by integrating sparse and dense representations within a decoder-only framework.

stories.title: Who Should Be Generated? Justifying Demographic Targets in Open-Ended Generation
stories.author: Wenqing Chen
bullet_points: The paper addresses a gap in fairness evaluation for open-ended generative models, focusing on output-side demographic composition.
Current fairness definitions often rely on input-side sensitive attributes, which doesn't fully capture generative bias.
The core issue identified is the lack of justification for the demographic targets used when auditing model outputs (e.g., generating 'a CEO').

stories.title: LiveMem: Maintaining Memory State Continuity in Long-Running LLM Inference
stories.author: Yang Xu
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of maintaining persistent state in long-running LLM agents whose input context is limited.
Introduces the concept of 'state continuity under context turnover' to manage computation across context changes.
Proposes a method (LiveMem) to carry forward a persistent memory state independent of the active context window.

stories.title: SWE-Touch: Benchmarking Coding Agents When Users Touch the Code
stories.author: Kang Liu
bullet_points: Introduces SWE-Touch, a new framework designed to benchmark coding agents in realistic, shared development environments.
Addresses a gap in current benchmarks by testing how agents handle code modifications made by human users during an active task.
Utilizes 'Counter-Edits' to simulate plausible, real-world code changes, moving beyond simple message-based interactions.

stories.title: Cultural Awareness is Represented but Not Decoded: Tracing Mythological Knowledge across 18 Open-Source LLMs
stories.author: Mika Hämäläinen
bullet_points: The study investigates how cultural knowledge, specifically mythological figures, is encoded across 18 open-source LLMs.
LLMs show a strong bias toward well-represented Western myths (e.g., Zeus, Jupiter) but struggle with less-represented traditions (e.g., Finnish, Egyptian).
Researchers used advanced probing techniques (linear probing, logit lens) to trace where this cultural default knowledge resides within the model architecture.

stories.title: IP and DNS Leaks in WebKit Affecting Proxy Browsers and iCloud Private Relay
stories.author: lapcat
bullet_points: WebKit vulnerabilities allow IP and DNS leaks.
The issue specifically impacts proxy browsers and iCloud Private Relay.
This represents a significant privacy and security concern for Apple users.

stories.title: Pass the Passkey: A Novel Attack Surface in Passwordless Authentication
stories.author: jchanimal
bullet_points: The article discusses a novel attack vector targeting passwordless authentication systems.
The vulnerability is related to the 'passkey' mechanism, suggesting a security flaw in modern authentication.
This represents a moderate but significant security concern in the rapidly evolving landscape of passwordless logins.

stories.title: Mana: 2-3 Seconds to Feeling Human
stories.author: yuuzulight
bullet_points: Development of a voice AI assistant running entirely locally on the user's machine.
Key feature is the elimination of cloud dependencies, APIs, and associated latency.
The project aims for a near-instantaneous, 'human-like' response time (2-3 seconds).

stories.title: Self-Hosting AI Models on a Raspberry Pi 5: A Complete Guide to Free, Private, Local AI Inference
stories.author: trismegistus
bullet_points: Guide details how to run AI models locally on a Raspberry Pi 5.
Utilizes Ollama to enable free, private, and local AI inference.
Highlights the benefits of zero API fees and complete data privacy.
